title: Readiness Signals
summary: Four questions before AI — clear steps, repetition, data, human review

sections.heading: Orientation — Beginning of the Lesson
sections.subtitle: Beginning of the Lesson
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What Will You Understand? AI works best when the process is clear — steps, data, repetition, and review limits.
- Why Now? Customer follow-up is designed. Before automation or delegation, you need to ensure the process itself is ready.
- What After the Lesson? You will choose one process and examine it: Is it clear? Is it repetitive? Does it have data? Does it need human review?

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Many say, "Let’s make AI do everything" — then they find every response is wrong because the steps are not agreed upon.
- AI does not fix operational chaos. It speeds up an existing process — if the process is unclear, it speeds up the mistake.
- Process Readiness means: knowing the steps, knowing what data is needed, and knowing where human review is required.

sections.heading: Core Idea — 4 Questions Before Adding AI
sections.subtitle: 4 Questions Before Adding AI
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Are the steps clear? — Can you write the process in 5–7 steps without "means" and "depends on the situation"?
- Is the process repetitive? — Does it happen every week or more — not a unique case once a year?
- Is there enough data? — Names, dates, prices, templates — AI needs clear inputs.
- Human review? — Sensitive decisions (price, major complaint, contract) must be approved by a human even if AI drafted the response.

sections.contentMarkdown: Readiness signals — a simple check. If there is a weak point in the four questions — fix the process first, then add AI.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: The process "Responding to Price Inquiries" — each time in a different style and no price list. Is it ready for AI?
No — the steps and data are unclear; the template and prices need to be standardized first
Explanation: Without standardized prices and templates, AI produces inconsistent responses. Readiness = clarity of the process.

sections.heading: Mission — Check the Readiness of One Process
sections.subtitle: Check the Readiness of One Process
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Choose one process in your work (follow-up, responding to complaints, pricing, weekly report). Answer the four questions honestly — not what you wish. Automation is not required — diagnosis is required. Submission: Name of the process · Clarity of steps · Repetition · Data · Human review · Judgment of ready/not ready with reasoning. Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Honest Check | 60% | A real process with answers to the four questions — not general |
| Clear Judgment | 40% | A ready/not ready decision with logical reasoning |
